what_this_lane_repairs.defect: An evidence-plane pick could not be settled at all. recordPickSettlement refuses anything but a posted pick, and a Track Only pick never becomes posted — by construction, because Track Only means there is no delivery to post. So an operator holding a real, graded result had no way to record it, and the four real production picks in the governed cohort had no path to a settled record.
what_this_lane_repairs.why_a_separate_dispatch_rather_than_a_lo: The posted-state guard is what stops a settlement being recorded against a pick that was never delivered. Loosening it would have removed the protection for every pick rather than adding a path for the evidence plane. The dispatch is placed deliberately AFTER the manual_review branch: an evidence-plane pick has no delivery to pause, and recordManualReview refuses anything but posted, so moving the dispatch above it would silently convert that refusal into an acceptance. A manual_review request on a Track Only pick must keep failing exactly as it does today, and a dedicated test asserts that it does.
what_this_lane_repairs.fail_closed_shape: recordOperatorEvidenceSettlement throws ApiError(400, OPERATOR_GRADING_CONTEXT_REQUIRED) when request.operatorGradingContext is absent, and ApiError(409, OPERATOR_SETTLEMENT_SOURCE_INVALID) when the caller claims source 'grading'. An operator settling by hand must attest, in their own words, how they determined the outcome, where a reader can independently check it, and when they observed it. A refusal writes no settlement row.
what_this_lane_repairs.no_lifecycle_transition_and_no_delivery: validated -> settled is not a legal FSM edge, so the operator path returns lifecycleEvent: null and finalLifecycleState: pick.status — the pick's status does not move. The recap guard in settle-pick-controller.ts is widened to skip an evidence-plane pick outright. That guard is enforcement rather than optimisation: today a recap on a Track Only pick is structurally inert because resolveRecapChannel requires a sent distribution_outbox row, but that is the absence of a delivery record, not a refusal to deliver.

unit_tests.label: The operator grading context contract: a fully attested context is accepted; each of outcomeBasis, resultSourceUrl and observedAt is refused when missing and when whitespace-only; an unparseable observedAt is refused as not an ISO-8601 instant; a settlement request WITHOUT the context is still valid (the requirement depends on the pick, which the validator cannot see); and a malformed context fails the whole settlement request.

Seven new tests plus the pre-existing delivery-path suite unchanged. The new ones: the happy path (source 'operator', no lifecycle event, status stays 'validated', zero distribution_outbox rows across ALL statuses, payload and audit-action assertions); refusal without a context writes no settlement row; a malformed context is refused; source 'feed' still 409s; source 'grading' is refused on this path; manual_review on a Track Only pick is STILL refused — the dispatch-order control; awaiting_approval also settles through the operator path; and a posted pick still settles without any operator context.

what_it_proves: A real Track Only pick, submitted through submitPickController against real PostgREST, is settled by an operator and produces EXACTLY ONE settlement_records row, read back from the database rather than from a return value: source='operator', settled_by='t1-proof-operator', the operatorGradingContext persisted in the payload, clv null and clvUnavailableReason 'operator_evidence_settlement_has_no_event_scope'.
picks.status is still 'validated' after the settlement — no lifecycle transition was attempted, and 0 pick_lifecycle rows carry to_state='settled'.
ZERO distribution_outbox rows exist for the pick, counted across every status rather than only the ones a delivery would use. This is the directive's 'prove zero delivery', measured in the database.

Without operatorGradingContext the settlement is refused and ZERO settlement_records rows exist, the pick status is unchanged, and there are still zero outbox rows. The fail-closed path is proven by absence in the database, not by an exception type.
runtime_proof.why_this_suite_and_not_the_in_memory_one: The in-memory bundle can be satisfied by a repository that never writes. Reading the row back from Postgres is what distinguishes 'the code returned an object' from 'a row exists', and counting outbox rows in SQL is what distinguishes 'no delivery was requested' from 'a delivery was requested and silently dropped'.

After this lands, a Command Center settlement of a Track Only pick is refused with OPERATOR_GRADING_CONTEXT_REQUIRED.
command_center_follow_up.is_this_a_regression: No. Today the same click is refused with SETTLEMENT_NOT_ALLOWED, because the pick is not posted. The refusal changes identity, not existence.

dependency_record.for_c2_and_ticket_level_statistics: A settled evidence-plane pick now has a settlement_records row whose payload carries operatorGradingContext, correction:false, evidencePlane:true, operatorSettled:true, the pick provenance payload, the stake-integrity payload, profitLossUnits for win/loss/push, and clv:null with an explicit clvUnavailableReason. Any statistics layer built over this cohort can therefore distinguish an operator-attested settlement from a graded one by payload rather than by inference, and can report CLV as unavailable-by-construction rather than as missing data.
